mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between GDPC1 drops and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over three months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over two months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between HOUST declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors seek higher returns in equities.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1%, or if the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven signal where a simultaneous increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 0.5% and 100,000 respectively within a month signals a significant labor market downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases > 0.5% and PAYEMS decreases > 100k in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS changes on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where a decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month during a period of economic expansion signals a weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances during economic expansion despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during expansionary periods.
